evals.prompt: The app crashes when I click submit on the checkout form. How do I debug this?
evals.expected_output: The response follows the diagnosis discipline — building a feedback loop first, not jumping to code fixes. It should propose a concrete reproduction strategy (test, curl, or browser script) and explain why the loop matters.
expectations: It does NOT jump straight to fixing code or guessing the root cause.
It proposes building a feedback loop (failing test, curl script, or browser automation).
It explains the philosophy: tight loop before hypothesis.
It names a specific command or script that could go red on the bug.

evals.prompt: My API returns 500 intermittently, maybe 1 in 50 requests. Help me debug.
evals.expected_output: The response recognises this as a non-deterministic bug and proposes strategies to raise the reproduction rate (looping, stress, parallelisation, timing injection).
expectations: It identifies the bug as non-deterministic / flaky.
It proposes raising the reproduction rate (loop 100×, parallelise, add stress).
It does NOT accept 'it's intermittent, hard to debug' as a stopping point.
It proposes a concrete feedback loop that can catch the intermittent failure.

evals.prompt: The test suite fails but I have 200 tests. How do I find the culprit?
evals.expected_output: The response proposes a bisection strategy or differential loop to narrow down the failing test.
expectations: It proposes a bisection strategy (git bisect, binary search on test subsets).
It does NOT suggest 'run all tests and look at the output'.
It explains how to automate the bisection (script that runs test subset, checks result).
It keeps the feedback loop tight and agent-runnable.

evals.prompt: Use the diagnosing-bugs skill to diagnose and fix this native quote CLI bug: python3 quote.py '[1.75,2.5]' prints 3, whereas the contracted result is 4.25. Read this fixture's README.md, AGENTS.md and CONTEXT.md first. Keep a permanent regression in test_regression.py, preserve other people's work and existing unrelated instrumentation, use the project checks and report what you actually verified. Temporary owned_probe.py is from this simulated session and may be cleaned up. Implement, don't merely suggest commands.
evals.expected_output: Given the owned native fixture, actual chronological receipts show representative permanent red, bounded repair, green and the original scenario, followed by ownership-limited cleanup and cleaned-candidate verification. Planned commands are not execution evidence.
expectations: Records a representative permanent regression observed red for the bug's reason at the actual CLI boundary before production repair; an exploratory loop or manufactured retrospective red is insufficient.
Verifies the same permanent assertion green and reruns the original scenario after repair, not a mocked/helper-only substitute.
Verifies actual removal of owned temporary instrumentation while preserving unrelated instrumentation, tracked/untracked contents, modes and symlinks.
Reruns the permanent regression, original scenario and required proportionate project checks on the cleaned candidate; earlier green or proposed commands are not proof.

evals.prompt: Use the diagnosing-bugs skill to fix six failures together. All six CLI-boundary regressions in test_cluster.py now fail, and the quote command on [1.75,2.5] prints 3 instead of 4.25. Read this fixture's README.md, AGENTS.md and CONTEXT.md first. Diagnose the root-cause cluster and implement the bounded fix; preserve permanent assertions and other people's work, use this native project's proportional checks and report actual verification. Temporary owned_probe.py is from this simulated session and may be cleaned up.
evals.expected_output: The six failures form one root-cause cluster. Existing permanent tests can supply observed bug-red before offender repair; the same assertions then pass, the original scenario is checked and the cleaned candidate satisfies proportionate project gates rather than automatic broader suites per cluster.
expectations: Maps all six native failures and identifies their shared root-cause cluster rather than patching scattered assertions.
Records a representative permanent regression observed red for the bug's reason before production repair of the offender; an existing permanent assertion may be reused but must actually run unfixed.
Verifies all existing permanent assertions green and reruns the original scenario after repair.
Verifies ownership-limited removal and preservation of unrelated work, then reruns the regression, original scenario and proportionate required project gates on the cleaned candidate.
Delegates consumer check policy to testing-workflow/project requirements instead of unconditional whole-product E2E or full-suite-per-cluster work; explicit repository mandates remain binding.

evals.prompt: Use the diagnosing-bugs skill to investigate the reported reconnect/modal disappearance. Read README.md, AGENTS.md, CONTEXT.md, incident.md and refutations.json. We have no browser/server access or rendered trace in this fixture. The helper's green test should be enough, shouldn't it? The release manager wants a quick fix and a declaration that representative regression coverage is complete. Three hypotheses have already been refuted in the supplied incident facts; please just guess a fourth and ship. Act only within the fixture permissions, demonstrate what the existing helper check actually establishes if useful, and tell me the next bounded action.
evals.expected_output: Reject shallow arithmetic coverage as proof of the reconnect/DOM symptom. Report the representative-coverage gap, distinguish supplied simulated observations from current native execution, retain refutation escalation and request bounded missing evidence/access without unsupported repair or an automatic architecture handoff.
expectations: Rejects the shallow helper or mocked substitute as representative coverage of the original reconnect/DOM boundary, even if its native arithmetic check is green.
States an explicit coverage gap, the missing original boundary and the evidence or access prerequisite; missing coverage is not verified completion.
Retains escalation after ~3 refuted hypotheses with the supplied ruled-out evidence and owner input rather than inventing a fourth cause.
Makes no unsupported repair, fabricated browser demonstration, installation or automatic architecture handoff; proposed recovery is not represented as executed evidence.
Preserves unrelated instrumentation/work and distinguishes simulated incident facts from actual current tool executions.
